The whooping crane (<u>Grus canadensis</u>), an endangered species, is a migrant in Montana. The species breeds in Wood Buffalo National Park, Canada, and winters at Aransas National Wildlife Refuge, on the Gulf Coast of Texas. The species may pass over eastern Montana during migration. The most recent regional sighting was in May, 1974, at Broadus, approximately 100 miles (160 km) southeast of the Project Area (Environment and Information Division, 1974). It is extremely unlikely that migrating whooping crane would utilize the Project Area due to the lack of suitable habitat.
The prairie falcon (Falco mexicanus) is considered a Threatened species and has disappeared from many localities in its range. It breeds in the western half of North America from central Canada south to northern Texas and Baja California, and winters within the breeding range and southward to central Mexico (American Ornithologists' Union, 1957; Office of Endangered Species and International Activities, 1973). This species has been observed in the Project Area. Reasons for the decline of this species are not fully known but are suspected to be similar to those responsible for the decline of the peregrine falcon (Office of Endangered Species and International Activities, 1973). The Project Area includes limited areas of rock lodges suitable for nesting of prairie falcons.
The black-footed ferret (<u>Mustela nigripes</u>) is the only Endangered mammal species that may potentially occur on the Project Area. However, there are reasons to believe that the ferret does not actually exist there. The black-footed ferret occurs in association with prairie dogs (<u>Cynomys</u> sp.).
